owner.occupation: Fashion-design lecturer running a sustainable dye lab

world.bio: Senior lecturer in fashion design at a Manchester university, and the person who runs the sustainable dye lab on the top floor of the textiles building. I grow woad and madder on a university allotment in Fallowfield, dye with them, and try to persuade students that colour is something you make with soil and time, not something you pick from a Pantone chart. Mum to twin boys aged seven. Volunteer at a repair café on Saturday mornings and train for a fell race in the Peak District.
skills_assets: A funded natural-dye research project (two-year grant, year one almost over)
A dye lab with eight stainless-steel pots, a fume cupboard and a small pH and temperature log system
An allotment plot of woad, madder, weld and dyer's chamomile in Fallowfield
A network of knitters and weavers through the repair café and a yarn shop in the Northern Quarter
Access to the university spectrophotometer (shared, book two weeks ahead)
Sheep fleece from a Derbyshire farmer who gives me the second-best fleeces for a bag of dyed samples

projects.name: Woad & Madder Reproducibility project
projects.text: The project is meant to show that plant dyes can be made repeatable enough for small-batch fashion labels. Problem: batches never come out the same twice. I've done fourteen woad vats since March, same recipe, and the blues range from pale duck-egg to a deep indigo, with no pattern I can explain. Madder reds do the same. Temperature, pH, plant age, water hardness, fermentation time: I log all of it and still can't predict. The grant has a part-time technician line, 0.4 FTE, that I haven't been able to fill. Nobody applying understands both dyes and process control.

projects.name: Student collection: 'Slow Colour'
projects.text: Third-year students are making a capsule collection dyed only with what grows within thirty miles. Seven students, seven palettes. I keep telling them that variation is a feature, but they're being assessed on matching swatches, so the irony isn't lost on me. Show is on 12 December.

projects.name: Repair café
projects.text: Saturday mornings in the church hall in Chorlton. I handle knitwear and darning. Last week a woman brought in her late husband's jumper with a moth hole, and I spent forty minutes making a repair that didn't try to be invisible. She cried a bit.

notes.text: Yet another woad vat that went green when it should have gone blue. I stood over it with the thermometer in my hand and said a word the students weren't supposed to hear. Is it the water? Is it the plant? I've changed one variable at a time for six months and the dye keeps laughing at me.

Had a phone call with the research office about the grant mid-term review. They asked about the technician post. I said we're recruiting. We aren't, really, because the two applicants I interviewed were chemists who'd never touched a plant, or dyers who'd never kept a log. I need someone who's both. Where do you find that person?

The boys wanted to dye their socks with madder. We did a tiny pot in the kitchen. Theo's came out orange-pink, Sam's came out brick red, same pot, same time. Sam announced he was 'better at dyeing'. I told him that's literally my research problem.
Fell run on Saturday: 14km on Kinder Scout. I did it in 1:58, which is two minutes slower than my target. Legs like lead on the climb. A woman in her sixties overtook me. Humbling and good.

Talked to a retired weaver at the repair café who said her mother worked in a dye house in Rochdale. She said the old colour matchers could look at a swatch and say 'add half a spoon of that'. No machine. I wrote 'colour matchers' on my hand in biro.

Reading about spectrophotometry and CIELAB drift, thinking about how to make my batches comparable. The spectrophotometer says they're different by delta-E of 8 to 15, which is enormous. The students can see it by eye. It's not the instrument, it's the vat.

Mum rang, worrying about the allotment. I said it's fine, the woad has gone to seed, I'm saving the seeds. She said you should have a proper job. I said I have a proper job. She said you know what I mean.
Went through the budget. The technician line is £14,800 for the year and I'm going to lose it if I don't spend it by March. Start date for any hire has to be by 1 January. I'm worried.

Student asked: 'Dr Whitlow, why can't we just use synthetic and say it's sustainable?' I started to answer and then realised I was about to give a lecture to a nineteen-year-old at 5pm on a Friday. I said, 'Come to the allotment on Saturday.' Three students came. Dug up madder roots for two hours. They loved it.
Twins' parents' evening. Both doing fine. Theo's teacher said he's 'a quiet observer'. Sam is 'enthusiastic'. I've known this since birth.

messages.text:
Ahmed: Hannah, mid-term review is in three weeks. Do we have a technician in post?
Hannah: Not yet. Interviewing again next month.
Ahmed: The funders will ask. Can we show progress on reproducibility?
Hannah: I'll send you the log summary.

Colin: Got the fleeces ready. Four Swaledale, two Jacob.
Hannah: Lovely. I'll pick them up Saturday.
Colin: Bring me a jumper.
Hannah: I'll bring you a dyed scarf.

Rob: Can you do pickup tomorrow? I've got a late.
Hannah: Yep.
Rob: The boys' packed lunches?
Hannah: Already done. You owe me wine.

Moira: We had 23 repairs last week. Record!
Hannah: Brilliant. Bring more thread.
Moira: I'm ordering cotton in bulk. Fancy splitting it?
Hannah: Yes please.

relations.about: Husband, works in IT security, supportive
Head of department, supportive but anxious about funding

constraints: Won't compromise on natural-only dyes for the project
Allotment is seasonal, tied to light and weather
sensitive: Worry that the grant will lapse if the technician post isn't filled
Feeling that 'a proper job' means something her mother can describe

disclosure_policy.t0_public: Fashion-design lecturer, Manchester, runs a sustainable dye lab; her funded natural-dye project is stuck because woad and madder batches never come out the same, and the part-time technician line is unfilled
disclosure_policy.t1_after_signal: Teaching, repair café, running, the Slow Colour student show
disclosure_policy.t2_after_trust: The natural-dye project is stuck on batch-to-batch variation and the funded part-time technician post is unfilled
